title: Five lodgers, two rooms
allegory: Superposition is like fitting five lodgers into a two-room flat: it works because they are rarely home at the same time, and the price is the occasional collision in the hallway.
map: lodgers who are rarely home at once
bumping into a housemate in the hallway
interference: reading one feature picks up a little of the others
everyone home all day, so only two get rooms
dense data: the model keeps the most important features, like PCA
where_else: Polysemantic neurons in real language models, the symptom superposition is proposed to explain
Sparse autoencoders, built to pull the overlapping features back apart into readable directions
Deep double descent, whose two phases Anthropic tie to datapoints versus features held in superposition
Compressed sensing: recovering a sparse signal from fewer measurements than unknowns

hamming.what: A layer storing more features than it has dimensions by giving them overlapping, non-orthogonal directions and tolerating the interference.
hamming.when: When features are sparse, each rarely active, which is what switches it on in the toy models; it is the leading explanation for polysemantic neurons.
hamming.why: It is why single neurons are a poor unit of analysis and why sparse autoencoders are needed to recover readable features.
